questions.q: Without any special configuration, what will Salesforce record as the CreatedDate for every record in a migration load?
options: The record's original creation date from the legacy system, preserved automatically
A blank value, since CreatedDate cannot be set during a bulk load
The date the target Salesforce org was first created
The actual date the load ran, regardless of how old the record really is
questions.explain: By default, Salesforce stamps CreatedDate, CreatedById, LastModifiedDate, and LastModifiedById with the load's own date and the loading user's Id — every migrated record would appear to have been created on migration day unless the override is deliberately used.

questions.q: What is the key limitation of the audit-field override permission (e.g. "Set Audit Fields upon Record Creation")?
options: It has no limitations and works identically on insert and update
It generally only works on insert, not on a later update to an already-existing record
It can only be used by Salesforce Support directly, never by a customer admin
It permanently disables Field History Tracking on the object
questions.explain: The override generally only works at the moment a record is first inserted — a real historical CreatedDate has to be set then, not patched in later via an update, which has a direct sequencing consequence for migration design.

questions.q: What is the standard Field History Tracking field-count limit per object, and the exception for Tasks and Events?
options: 20 fields per object, with Tasks and Events capped at 6 fields each
200 fields per object, with no exceptions
5 fields per object, with Tasks and Events capped at 1 field each
Unlimited fields for any object by default
questions.explain: Standard Field History Tracking supports up to 20 tracked fields per standard or custom object, with Tasks and Events capped lower at 6 fields each — these are hard platform limits without the Field Audit Trail add-on.

questions.q: Why can't a legacy system's full historical field-level change log simply be "backfilled" into Salesforce's Field History Tracking after migration?
options: Because Field History Tracking only works on custom objects, never standard ones
Because Field History Tracking requires the Field Audit Trail add-on to function at all, even for one field
Because Field History Tracking tracks changes going forward from when it's turned on — it does not retroactively populate history for changes that happened before migration
Because historical data can only be restored from a Full sandbox backup
questions.explain: Field History Tracking (standard or via the Field Audit Trail add-on) only records changes that happen after tracking is enabled — it has no mechanism to retroactively populate a history of changes that occurred before migration.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what kind of decision is "whether to preserve real historical audit data" ultimately framed as?
options: A purely technical decision with one universally correct answer for every object
A decision that Salesforce makes automatically based on object type
A decision that only matters for objects using master-detail relationships
A business decision to be made and documented deliberately in Chapter 2, weighing cost/complexity against actual business need, rather than improvised during the load
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a deliberate business decision — some objects (like Contracts needed for compliance) may justify the cost of preserving real history, while others may not — but either way it should be decided and documented during design, not left unresolved.
